A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenFly and retain the same central platform, dataset, and navigation-agent research. All 20 pages of v6 and 21 pages of v7, including appendices, are readable; visual inspection resolves figure and table content sufficiently for comparison.

before.justification: V6 reports original navigation benchmarks, component ablations, dataset analyses, and experiments on 23 real-world tasks in Appendix K.

after.justification: V7 reports original navigation benchmarks, expanded ablations, attention visualizations, and the retained 23-task real-world evaluation in Section 6.4.

M1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 introduce a trained landmark-grounding head with three cross-attention layers and GIoU supervision. Bounding-box area now governs keyframe retention, and the largest-box frame replaces the first frame as the token-merging reference. V7 also adds DAgger augmentation as a platform capability. The instruction-generation change from one to three images in the main text matches v6 Appendix F and does not independently establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Figure 3 revise the dataset's reported flight-height coverage from 0–150 m to 0–210 m. The 100K trajectories, 18 scenes, four rendering engines, and 23 real-world tasks remain. This establishes a limited revision of reported flight conditions, without establishing new data collection.

E2.justification: V7 Table 2 adds See-Point-Fly to the test-unseen comparison. Random, Seq2Seq, CMA, AerialVLN, Navid, and NaVila remain. The real-world comparator set remains Navid and NaVila.

E3.justification: The added See-Point-Fly evaluation uses GPT-4.1 zero-shot on test-unseen, and the expanded ablation introduces uniform-history and random-candidate selection controls. The stated 1,800/1,200 seen/unseen split sizes and 20 m success threshold remain. Newly documented screening, collision handling, and training hyperparameters do not establish that earlier experiments used different settings.

E4.justification: V7 Table 3 extends the existing component ablation with History and Random KS controls, testing uniform sampling and random selection within candidate keyframes. Appendix I adds attention maps with and without VTM in Figure 13. Existing success and failure cases remain, with added landmark-grounding annotations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for navigation performance. The 3K-sample quality inspection and 25-instruction linguistic analysis retain their sampling descriptions.

E6.justification: V6 Table 1 to v7 Table 2 replaces nearly all non-random benchmark scores: OpenFly's seen/unseen SR changes from 33.2%/10.7% to 34.3%/22.6%, and NaVila's from 14.2%/4.5% to 20.3%/14.7%. Ablation scores and result entries also change. These are revised reported results, not an isolated same-setting gain. Real-world scores remain unchanged. The relocated dataset-statistics table drops REVERIE, CVDN, LANI, and ANDH rows.

T1.justification: Appendix E retains the same voxel/BEV maps, landmark-height condition, and path-search reasoning. Neither version contains substantive theoretical guarantees or proofs. V7's bounding-box notation and named GIoU objective do not introduce a new formal derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about the automatic platform, largest 100K-trajectory aerial benchmark, and superior navigation agent remain. V7's abstract and introduction additionally make computational savings and advantages over uniform frame sampling explicit. Numerical success-rate margins and real-world evidence receive greater prominence without introducing a new research objective.

C2.justification: V7 removes v6 Section 7's substantive limitations concerning large-scene reconstruction artifacts and impractical real-time onboard deployment. It adds an explanation that excessive visual tokens dilute cross-modal attention, supported by the new attention visualization, and discusses compatibility with on-policy training and different planning/control systems. Unseen-scene degradation and qualitative failure cases remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: V7 newly specifies batch size 64, learning rate 2e-5, the grounding loss and area threshold, complete test-set inspection, collision-as-failure handling, and Super/MPC planning and control. It omits v6's explicit encoder resolution, projection-layer description, vertical/turn action-unit specifications, and project-page link. These are mixed documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding changes to every underlying setting or resource.

R1.justification: V7 substantially updates the cited landscape with CityNavAgent, See-Point-Fly, GeoNav, EO-1, trajectory-planning/DAgger references, and token-sparsification work. Section 2.2 expands discussion of training-free methods and grounding limitations; earlier LAW, GridMM, topological-planning, and cross-modal-map references disappear. Appendix H also adds Wang et al. (2025a), whose listed ECG-generation title leaves its relevance to linguistic analysis unexplained.

P1.justification: The abstract and related-work narrative are rewritten, Section 3.1's separate engine descriptions are condensed, and dataset comparisons move into the main text. Implementation details and real-world experiments move from appendices into Section 6; the limitations section disappears and acknowledgement/LLM-use sections appear. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond formatting and renumbering.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are redrawn, including replacement of the joint trajectory histogram with separate distributions and consolidation of word clouds. V6's real-world Tables 6–7 become v7 Figure 5; snapshots are expanded and relocated. Qualitative figures gain grounding boxes, Figure 13 adds attention maps, and the dataset table is relocated and shortened. Typography, citation appearance, and page composition also change throughout.

improvement.justification: V7 makes the agent's training and test-time grounding procedure explicit, adds useful controls and attention evidence, and brings the ablation narrative into agreement with its table. These improve assessability. The gain is limited by removal of substantive reconstruction/deployment limitations and some reproducibility information, while widespread score replacements remain unexplained and cannot establish a controlled performance improvement.
